review_target.review_goal: Determine whether recursive polarity may be treated as an aspect-layer nested inside the broader continuation closure relation without introducing separable primitives.

supported_interpretations.statement: Recursive polarity may be provisionally interpreted as an aspect-pattern nested inside the continuation closure relation.
The nested expression preserves the indivisibility direction established by the Aspect Non-Separability Principle.
The expression remains admissible only when interpreted as simultaneous aspect relation rather than sequential composition.

unresolved_risks.statement: Nested ⇔R usage may create ambiguity between recursive aspect binding and hierarchical operator stacking.
The symbolic reuse of ⇔R at multiple nesting levels may accidentally imply associativity or transitivity not yet governed.
The nested form may tempt projection into physical or arithmetic interpretations beyond current governance.

provisional_constraints.simultaneity_rule: Nested relations must be interpreted as simultaneous aspect-preserving wholes, not ordered execution chains.
provisional_constraints.non_associativity_rule: No associativity or operator flattening may be inferred from nested ⇔R expressions.
provisional_constraints.non_transitivity_rule: A ⇔R B and B ⇔R C do not automatically imply A ⇔R C.
provisional_constraints.non_hierarchy_rule: Nested structure must not be interpreted as ontological hierarchy unless separately governed.

allowed_reading.statement: The candidate expression may be read as a recursively nested whole-relation in which exclusion, continuation, polarity, and residue-binding are treated as simultaneous aspects of one indivisible process structure.

forbidden_readings.statement: The expression proves a final unified ontology.
The expression replaces arithmetic or logic.
